notes:
Dynamic caption scenes add animated text, layered materials, pinned images and bounded image sequences through a shared preview/export format. This is a rendering foundation; a preset gallery is still pending.
Caption layout and timing support word, line, page and character animation, mixed font styles and duration-aware expressions, with fixes for page timing and whitespace geometry.
Caption materials add trails, blur, glow, waves, noise and gradient effects, while retaining independent layer blending against video.
Shorts preserve the full source picture when the canvas ratio changes, retain each shot’s focal point and support 100–400% zoom.
Free placement lets you drag, scale, align and nudge media into picture-in-picture without a visual jump.
Speech recognition, speech synthesis and image generation each have one default model picker covering local, remote, cloud and Agent models. Automatic image selection prefers subscription-based Codex.
Local image generation shows loading stages, sampling progress, elapsed time and estimates. Generated images open in the shared viewer.
Qwen-Image uses less memory on MLX through streamed layers, blockwise VAE loading and in-place chunks.
The local image API accepts seed and steps controls within each model’s limits; Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo keeps its fixed eight-step schedule.
Built-in skills show localized names and summaries. Video production supports opening samples, shot/timecode revisions and recorded narration.
Download cards remain visible after import, show saved files and sizes, and offer playback, Open with default app and Show in Folder.
Task details recover from rendering errors without taking down the interface.
Long transcripts support partial speaker, word and stable-ID edits, retaining revision checks and undo.
Exports check free space on the destination disk, stage there and clean up temporary task directories.
Export compositing, caption/effect caching and platform scheduling reduce redundant work and stalls. Performance depends on hardware and workload.
macOS packages are signed and notarized. Windows CPU, CUDA and Vulkan packages are unsigned and require the Microsoft Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable.
